thesis: Leading all-flash enterprise data storage provider formerly known as Pure Storage (PSTG), rebranded to Everpure in February 2026 with the single-letter NYSE ticker 'P' adopted in April 2026. FY2026 delivered $3.66B revenue (+15.6% YoY), gross margin expansion to 70.4%, and the first full year of GAAP profitability ($188.2M net income) alongside $690.6M free cash flow and a $2.39B cash balance. The Evergreen//One subscription model, AI data-pipeline positioning for FlashBlade, and the 1touch data-intelligence acquisition provide durable growth. After the post-rebrand spike faded, the stock has cooled to ~$80, roughly fair value within our base case. A ~$482M annual stock-based-compensation burden and a $2.78B convertible-note overhang remain the key dilution headwinds, keeping the risk/reward balanced.

drivers: Revenue grows at 20% CAGR through FY2030 driven by AI infrastructure demand
Operating margins expand to 22%+ as subscription mix increases and scale benefits accrue
1touch acquisition integration accelerates the data intelligence revenue stream
Evergreen//One subscription reaches 40%+ of revenue, driving multiple expansion

risks: Revenue growth slows to 10% CAGR due to cloud migration and competitive pressure
Operating margins stall at 14% due to pricing pressure and SBC inflation
Enterprise IT spending downturn compresses storage demand cyclically
Valuation compresses to 20x forward earnings on execution concerns

base_case.assumptions: Revenue grows at 15% CAGR through FY2030; gross margins stabilize at 69-71%; operating margins reach 18% by FY2030; subscription mix grows to 35% of revenue; FCF generation sustains $700M+ annually.

catalysts.event: Q2 FY2027 Earnings — subscription mix and post-rebrand growth validation
Everpure Investor Day — long-term strategic roadmap and margin targets
1touch integration milestone — data intelligence revenue contribution
Q3 FY2027 Earnings — full-year guidance update
Q4 and FY2027 Earnings — second full year of GAAP profitability

key_risks: $481.7M annual stock-based compensation (~13% of revenue) creates ongoing shareholder dilution
$2.78B convertible notes create potential future dilution if converted
Intense competition from Dell EMC, NetApp, HPE, and hyperscaler cloud storage
Enterprise storage is cyclical; a recession would materially impact demand
Storage is an AI enabler rather than a primary beneficiary; AI capex rotation toward compute could disappoint
